How pairs are selected

Each exact-model record needs at least three positive finite mechanical fields (peak torque, rated torque, maximum speed, mass), including torque. Pairs share at least three fields and the same drive category. Each eligible model proposes up to three nearest peers by mean relative difference across shared fields; ties use sorted IDs. Proposals are deduplicated, so incoming links can exceed three. This is a discoverability heuristic, not engineering compatibility or measured performance. Controller, bare-reducer, family/series and sparse records are excluded; zeros and nulls do not establish similarity. An authored evidence dossier takes precedence. Arbitrary gallery selections remain available but are not generated SEO pages.

Actuator selection guide

Sensor bits are not loaded accuracy. CAD geometry is not a calibrated simulation model. Thermal duty and efficiency require matched operating conditions.

CyberGear Micromotor / efficiency: scope & sources

Original CyberGear, 24 V / 7.75:1 / 317 g; not CyberGear 2.0

No complete bus-to-output efficiency map established in the reviewed original manual; its torque–speed curve is not efficiency.

Iq/phase current and bus voltage do not substitute for synchronized bus-power and output-torque measurements; regeneration and idle losses remain unknown.

  • Chinese manual (mirror): PDF pp4,6,15–16; parameter/telemetry tables; reviewed pp1–30
CyberGear Micromotor / thermal: scope & sources

Original CyberGear, 24 V / 7.75:1 / 317 g; not CyberGear 2.0

Vendor overload table includes 11 N·m/45 s, 10/60, 9/90, 7/320 at 24 rpm, 25 °C ambient and 120 °C winding endpoint.

120 °C is not a protection setting: board ceiling 80 °C, CAN default motor warning/fault 75/80 °C. Initial winding temperature, mounting/airflow, NTC-to-winding offset and repeat-cycle recovery are unknown; no cooldown inferred.

  • Chinese manual (mirror): PDF pp4–5 section 1.3.15 overload table; p6 board limit; p24 section 4.1.10 CAN defaults
CyberGear Micromotor / precision: scope & sources

Original CyberGear, 24 V / 7.75:1 / 317 g; not CyberGear 2.0
